name: str_replace_all
title: Replace every match with new text

origin.description: Replaces every match of a pattern in each string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A regular expression by default. A named vector, such as c(one = "1"), replaces each name with its value, in order. fixed() compares literal text and coll() uses collation. A boundary, including the empty string, is an error when replacement is text.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Usually one string, or a vector the same length as string or pattern. It is ignored when pattern is named. \1, \2, and so on insert capture groups. A function receives every match in one vector and must return character text of that same length.

origin.details: Every non-overlapping match is replaced. A named pattern is applied one pair at a time. A function sees the matches flattened into one vector; a missing value in its return makes that whole string missing. On the function path an empty pattern matches characters.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string, pattern, or replacement.
origin.example:
fruits <- c("one apple", "two pears", "three bananas")
writeLines(c(
  str_replace_all(fruits, "[aeiou]", "-"),
  str_replace_all(fruits, "[aeiou]", toupper),
  str_replace_all(fruits, "b", NA_character_),
  str_replace_all(paste(fruits, collapse = "---"), c(one = "1", two = "2", three = "3"))
))

translation.description: Replaces every match of a pattern in each string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings and stringi._na.NA. NULL is an empty list.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A string or list is an ICU regular expression. A dict, or a vector with a names attribute, is a sequence of pattern and replacement pairs. fixed, coll, and regex come from stringr.pattern.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings. It is unused when pattern is a dict or has names, and can be omitted in that case. A callable receives every match as one list and must return character text of that length.

translation.details: Text replacement calls stringi's all-replace functions. A callable flattens the matches with vctrs.list_unchop, cuts the result with 1-based ranges, and writes them with stri_sub_replace_all. A missing piece makes the whole string missing.
translation.value: A list of strings. Names on the input are kept when the pattern length is 1 or equals the string length.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringr.replace import str_replace_all

def toupper(match):
    return [NA if item is NA else item.upper() for item in match]

fruits = ["one apple", "two pears", "three bananas"]
rows = []
rows.extend(str_replace_all(fruits, "[aeiou]", "-"))
rows.extend(str_replace_all(fruits, "[aeiou]", toupper))
rows.extend(str_replace_all(fruits, "b", NA))
rows.extend(str_replace_all("---".join(fruits), {"one": "1", "two": "2", "three": "3"}))
for item in rows:
    print(item)
